commit.message:
fix(notifications): remove mark-all-read-on-leave, restore unread badge correctness (#4729) (#4758)

* fix(notifications): remove mark-all-read-on-leave, keep unread badge correct (#4729)

MarkAllReadOnDispose fired repository.markAllAsRead() whenever the user
left the notifications surface, optimistically zeroing the badge in a way
that fought the repository snapshot (the single source of truth) and made
unread state feel unreliable.

Remove the on-leave policy from both NotificationsPage and the inbox
scaffold and delete the widget. Unread now changes only on deliberate read
transitions — per-item tap (NotificationFeedItemTapped -> markAsRead) and
the explicit mark-all in notification settings. Realtime arrivals still
increment unread through the repository snapshot, which the badge cubit
subscribes to.

Tests invert the unmount assertions (leaving the screen must NOT mark all
read); per-item-read convergence (badge_converges_after_tap_read_back) and
realtime-arrival increment (repository acceptRealtime test) already pin the
badge contract.

* refactor(notifications): remove orphaned mark-all-read bloc event (#4729)

Removing MarkAllReadOnDispose left NotificationFeedMarkAllRead +
_onMarkAllRead with no UI dispatcher: the only live "mark all read" is
the notification settings screen, which calls repository.markAllAsRead()
directly. The bloc event/handler were dead code.

Delete the event, its bloc registration + handler, the onMarkAllRead
Reportable site, the three orphaned bloc tests, and the now-unused
markAllAsRead setUp stub. Reword the NotificationsPage doc so it no
longer implies a mark-all action exists on the feed surface.

No behavior change — per-item read (NotificationFeedItemTapped ->
markAsRead) and the settings mark-all path are untouched.

commit.message:
fix(notifications): suppress duplicate local push render on iOS alert pushes (#4731) (#4760)

* fix(notifications): suppress duplicate local push render on iOS alert pushes (#4731)

divine-push-service builds an APNS aps.alert (+ content_available) for
every push (fcm_sender.rs build_apns_config, merged in #17). On iOS
background/terminated the OS presents that alert AND content_available
wakes the background isolate, which then built a second, local
notification — two banners for one push. Android stays data-only
(notification:None) so it never double-rendered.

Guard _firebaseMessagingBackgroundHandler to render a local notification
only for data-only messages. FlutterFire surfaces the OS-presented alert
as RemoteMessage.notification, so shouldRenderLocalPushNotification()
returns false whenever it is set; tapping the OS banner still routes via
onMessageOpenedApp / getInitialMessage (message.data) unchanged.

Foreground is unaffected (no setForegroundNotificationPresentationOptions,
so iOS does not OS-present in foreground; the app stays the sole renderer
there). Client-side defensive fix per #4731; payload contract tracked in
divine-push-service#20.

* refactor(notifications): tighten push de-dup guard clarity and tests (#4731)

Self-review polish on the #4760 duplicate-push fix (no behavior change to
shouldRenderLocalPushNotification):

- Move title/body extraction below the render guard so we don't build
  display strings for messages we drop, and don't read data['body'] twice.
- Reframe the helper doc: the data-only iOS branch is defensive (the push
  service always sends aps.alert today); rendering happens on Android.
- Cover the predicate's edges (empty-string body, non-String body,
  OS-alert-with-no-data-body) and document that the handler's early-return
  is verified on-device, not in unit tests.

commit.message:
refactor(ui): extract NotificationSettingsScreen widgets and drop dead toggles (#4780)

Replace the _buildSectionHeader/_buildNotificationCard/_buildActionCard/
_buildInfoCard helper methods with small private widget classes, and drop
the four local-only toggles (system, push, sound, vibration): they never
persisted and nothing consumed them. NotificationPreferences (the kind 3083
push contract) has no slot for them, so they were no-op switches that misled
users into thinking they did something.

Icons now use DivineIcon from the design system instead of raw Icons.*,
mirroring the canonical notificationTypeIconSpec mapping (heart/chat/user/
repeat); the app-bar refresh action uses SvgIconSource(arrowClockwise).

Removes the 9 now-unused notificationSettings* l10n keys across all 18
locales and regenerates. Adds a toggle-persists test and reveals the
mark-all-as-read card with ensureVisible in the two snackbar tests (the
shorter screen now lands it at the viewport fold).

commit.message:
refactor(models): extract URL resolution out of VideoEvent (#4748)

* refactor(models): extract URL resolution out of VideoEvent

Move the 5 URL-resolution methods (isValidVideoUrl, scoreVideoUrl,
selectBestVideoUrl, extractVideoUrlFromContent, findAnyVideoUrlInTags) out of
the VideoEvent data model into a dedicated, tested VideoUrlResolver utility in
the same package. URL selection is business logic, not data, so it should not
live on the model.

Behavior-preserving: methods moved verbatim; the only consolidation is the
apt.openvine.co -> api.openvine.co typo fix (previously duplicated across 3
methods) now in one private helper. The existing VideoEvent parsing/json/
filters tests (which exercise the factory delegating to the resolver) stay
green, and the resolver gains 26 direct unit tests it never had as private
methods. video_event.dart drops ~144 lines.

Part of #4338 (Wave 2). Closes #4740.

* refactor(models): finish video URL typo normalization cleanup

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>
